purpose: Implement live session skill management with an initial developer-role catalog snapshot, append-only upsert/revoke deltas, on-demand versioned SKILL.md bodies, authoritative execution-time validation, and high prompt-cache prefix reuse.

accepted_design.authority: The revisioned Effective Skill Registry is authoritative. Prompt history is only a model-visible projection and never grants execution permission.
invocation_order: current user input or Skill tool call
catalog_events: upsert for add, metadata/content/visibility update, and re-enable
revoke for disable, delete, or permission loss

management_ui.entry: Exact /skills immediately opens one searchable checklist with status, name, summary, source, path, visibility, mutability, and scope. Explicit /skills subcommands continue through the text command path.
management_ui.checkboxes: Every row shows configured visibility on the left: auto, name-only, and manual-only are [x], while off is [ ]. A configured-on row shadowed by a same-name winner stays [x] but its selected details identify the winner stable ID and explain that it is currently inactive. Opening the checklist does not reset persisted state.
management_ui.space_toggle: Space toggles only the selected skill between off and its last non-off visibility; when no prior non-off state exists, it restores auto.
management_ui.layout: Each skill item occupies exactly one terminal row and is ellipsized by terminal display-cell width. Only the selected skill renders a bounded detail block. The complete panel height, including both borders and optional chrome, never exceeds the current viewport and is recomputed on resize.
management_ui.scope: Interactive toggles persist as project-local overrides and apply immediately to the current session. An active session override blocks the shortcut with an actionable conflict instead of being silently replaced. Session-only and advanced visibility edits remain available through text commands.
management_ui.concurrency: Every Space mutation uses stable SkillID plus observed catalog revision and redraws from the authoritative result; stale rows are rejected and refreshed.

cache_rules: never rewrite the initial catalog in visible history
never generate one tool definition per skill
keep system instructions, tool definitions, and prompt cache key independent of catalog revision
treat compaction/new context epoch as an intentional one-time prefix rebuild
accepted_design.security_boundary: Disable/revoke immediately blocks future execution but cannot erase skill text already exposed to the model. Sensitive-content revocation requires a new or scrubbed context.

current_repo_findings: Current loop ordering is user input followed by a user-role skill listing; it must become developer catalog followed by user input.
Current Manager is primarily name-keyed and needs stable source-plus-locator identity to manage same-name skills correctly.
Current session enable/disable overlay is in-memory and boolean-only.
Current types.Message has no developer role.
Current announced skill state is not bound to visible context epoch, so compaction can leave an invalid cursor.
Current SkillTool already has a natural execution-time validation point and should remain the hard enforcement boundary.

concurrency_strategy.principle: Increase throughput by splitting pure contracts, catalog components, provider adapters, compact sub-pipelines, runtime surfaces, and acceptance lanes while giving each existing production file one owner.
conflict_controls: No two tasks in the same or different waves own the same existing production file.
Tasks add uniquely named taskNN test files instead of editing shared broad test files.
Integration and acceptance tasks modify tests/reports only; production defects return to the owning implementation task.
A dependent task starts only after every dependency is accepted.
If an owned production file contains unrelated dirty changes, preserve them and report overlap instead of overwriting.

waves.notes: Freeze the catalog value contract and transport-neutral developer message contract.
Build six independent pure catalog/storage/envelope components in new files.
Implement three provider projections, settings validation, MCP catalog inputs, and the pure loop coordinator.
Integrate the Manager and session state while two disjoint compact pipelines handle the new developer role.
Expose command/invocation contracts, enforce execution, and install pre-user query ordering.
Rebuild catalog state after every compact/recovery path and implement TUI/screen-reader surfaces in parallel.
Build the direct interactive skills checklist after its command and launcher contracts are stable.
Wire the completed component and surface contracts through root runtime composition.

Run the isolated skills-panel layout follow-up alongside already-independent integration/cache lanes; task_28 starts only after task_31 and then validates the combined lifecycle and visual contract without editing production code.
Final verifier runs all gates and publishes evidence without fixing production code. Its existing dependency on task_28 makes task_31 a transitive prerequisite.

required_scenarios: Initial full catalog snapshot is before the current user message.
No catalog change emits no catalog message.
Disable/delete emits revoke and execution rejects immediately.
Same-name skills from different sources remain separately manageable.
Session and persistent overrides remain isolated and survive only their intended lifecycle.
Resume/compact rebuild when catalog/body messages are absent from the visible context epoch.
Full SKILL.md content loads only on invocation and carries ID, revision, and digest.
Anthropic, OpenAI Chat, and OpenAI Responses preserve equivalent logical order.
System instructions, tool schemas, model settings, and PromptCacheKey remain stable across catalog revisions.
Internal developer catalog messages remain hidden from normal transcript presentation.
Exact /skills immediately opens a searchable checkbox list with no intermediate action menu; Enter is inert and one Esc closes it.
Effective non-off states render [x], off renders [ ], and explicit /skills subcommands continue through the text command path.

Space changes only the selected mutable stable ID, preserves its persisted last non-off visibility, rejects stale/session-overridden rows, and redraws from the authoritative result after success or failure.
Every skill list item occupies one terminal row and uses grapheme-safe terminal-cell ellipsis for ASCII, CJK, combining text, emoji/ZWJ sequences, and long metadata.
Only the selected skill exposes detail rows; selection and filtering remove the previous skill's details.
The complete skills panel, including top and bottom borders, stays inside the terminal viewport at extreme widths/heights and after shrink/grow resize.
Concurrent refresh, toggle, snapshot, and invoke are race-free.

dispatch_rules: Dispatch no more than six subagents concurrently, per workspace AGENTS.md.
Use the wave order unless a task's explicit dependencies permit a narrower safe advance.
Assign each task as a standalone prompt using its dispatch_prompt, read_first, owned_files, and verification fields.
Do not let integration, acceptance, or verifier tasks repair production code.
Do not merge task ownership because work appears small; the split is intentionally optimized for concurrent low-conflict execution.
Mark a task accepted only after its verification commands pass and its owned-file diff is reviewed.
Task status transitions are recorded by the external coordinator after verification; implementation agents do not edit task definition JSON unless explicitly assigned that bookkeeping.
